algorithm: Seeded geometric-growth business series; KPIs from period ratios: growth, churn, CAC, and LTV from ARPU over churn.
complexity: O(M) over M months of synthetic data; all KPI math is O(1) on aggregates.
data_flow_ascii:
seed -> generate_business_data (12 months: revenue, users, adds, churn, spend)
series -> compute_kpis -> growth rate, churn rate, CAC, LTV
series + KPIs -> sparkline + render_dashboard -> ASCII dashboard
description_sentence: A KPI dashboard that computes growth rate, churn, CAC, and LTV from seeded synthetic business data and renders an ASCII dashboard with sparklines.
failure_note: Zero new customers yields a reported CAC of infinity rather than a division crash, and flat series render flat sparklines.

functions.desc: Seeded 12-month synthetic series: revenue, users, adds, churn, spend.
functions.name: generate_business_data

functions.desc: Growth rate, churn rate, CAC, and LTV from the series.
functions.name: compute_kpis

functions.desc: Map a numeric series to unicode block sparkline characters.
functions.name: sparkline

functions.desc: Format the KPI values and sparklines as an ASCII dashboard.
functions.name: render_dashboard

functions.desc: Seeded demo: generate data, compute KPIs, print the dashboard.
functions.name: run_demo

functions.desc: Build the command-line parser for the demo.
functions.name: build_parser

functions.desc: Entry point: seeded KPI dashboard demo.
functions.name: main

label: kpi_dashboard
output_shape: Prints an ASCII dashboard box with four KPIs, monthly revenue/user sparklines, and the raw monthly table.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that turns raw business series into growth, churn, CAC, and LTV on one ASCII dashboard.

qa.a: Total marketing spend divided by total new customers; with zero new customers it reports infinity instead of crashing.
Average revenue per user divided by the churn rate, the standard payback-style lifetime estimate.
Yes: generate_business_data only makes the demo series; compute_kpis works on any dict with the same keys.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python computing growth, churn, CAC, and LTV from synthetic business data with an ASCII dashboard.
run_notes: --months sets the synthetic history length; values are seeded and reproducible.
scaling_note: In-memory series suit dashboard demos; production use would stream aggregates from a warehouse.
storage_note: No persistence: the series is regenerated from the seed on every run.
tradeoff_note: Synthetic data makes the demo reproducible but carries none of the messiness of real business metrics.
